name: Gray Leaf Spot
description: A serious fungal disease causing rectangular, gray to brown lesions along leaf veins. It thrives in warm, humid conditions and can cause significant yield loss.
symptoms: Rectangular, gray to tan lesions running parallel to leaf veins
Lesions coalescing in severe infections causing leaf blight
Symptoms appearing first on lower leaves and progressing upward
causes: Warm temperatures (22-30°C) with extended leaf wetness
Reduced-till or no-till farming without residue management
treatments: Apply strobilurin fungicides (azoxystrobin) at tasseling stage
Use triazole fungicides (propiconazole, tebuconazole) for curative treatment
Apply fungicide mixture for broad-spectrum control
prevention: Plant resistant hybrids with GLS tolerance
Rotate with non-cereal crops for 1-2 years
Bury crop residue through deep plowing
Optimize plant density to reduce canopy humidity
Use balanced fertilization to avoid excessive nitrogen
